# Google Meet Now Sends 1080p Video on the Web by Default: What It Means for You

> **In short:** Google says 1080p Full HD video sending in Google Meet on the web is now open to all users, and it is on by default on eligible computers. You can lower it anytime in Settings, under Video. The extended rollout started November 11, 2026.

Ever wondered why your face looks a little blurry on a video call while everyone else looks crisp? Video quality depends on settings, your camera, and your connection, and a change like this can quietly make your calls look better.

## What changed

Until now, sending full 1080p video in Meet on the web was limited to certain paid editions. Google says it is now available to all users. 1080p means a picture of 1920 by 1080 pixels (the tiny dots that make up an image), which is the standard "Full HD" level many newer cameras can capture.

Here is the important part. On a computer with a 1080p camera and enough processing power and internet speed, Google says 1080p is turned on automatically. You do not have to find a hidden switch to get it.

## How the sharper video behaves

Sharper video uses more of your computer's processing power and more of your internet connection. Google says Meet only sends 1080p when your video box, called a tile (the square that shows one person's camera), is large enough to show that detail. If your tile is small, there is no point sending extra pixels.

If your computer gets busy or your connection slows down, Meet automatically lowers the resolution. The call should keep going, just at a lower quality.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life**: If you join family calls or online classes from a laptop, you may notice a clearer picture without changing anything. If your computer feels slow during a call, you can lower the video quality in Settings, under Video.
- **For your business or work**: Administrators can set the default video quality for groups of users in the Admin console (the control panel for a Google Workspace organization). Google notes that existing bandwidth limits stay in place. Check your organization's policy before changing anything, because the admin setting can also restrict what users control.
- **If you're just getting started**: Open Meet on your computer and look in Settings under Video. Find the quality option and see what it says. Changing it is safe, and you can switch back at any time.
- **If you already use it**: If you share a single office network with many video users, watch whether calls stay smooth at 1080p. If they do not, ask your administrator whether the default can be changed for your group, or lower your own setting.

Google also says the rollout may take longer than 15 days before the feature is visible for everyone. So if your Meet still looks the same, give it some time.

## Wrap-up

The main news is simple: Google says 1080p video sending in Meet on the web is now open to everyone, and eligible computers use it by default, with automatic scaling when things get slow. Your next step is easy. Start your next video call on your computer, then open Settings and check the Video option so you know what your call is actually sending.
